news.title: FIFA's Infantino claims 'vast majority' support before election
news.lede: FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino said he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of football despite his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. Infantino is seeking re-election next year in the face of attempts to force him to stand down following the divisive plan. He infuriated football leaders in Europe, North America and Asia over the proposal to sell profits in the World Cup through a commercial subsidiary. But in an interview released on Saturday with the BBC at the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, Infantino brushed off calls for him to step down.

news.title: FIFA opens bidding for 2030 World Cup US rights: Netflix, Disney, Amazon joins race
news.lede: FIFA has formally opened the tender for U.S. and Puerto Rico media rights to the 2030 men’s World Cup, with bids due by November 19 and the winning partner expected to be chosen before the end of 2026. The tender is primarily for the 2030 tournament, which will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco. FIFA is also allowing bidders to submit combined offers for the 2034 World Cup, scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia.Interested broadcasters and streaming platforms can request the invitation to tender through FIFA’s dedicated media-rights email address. FIFA said the process is intended to select one or more partners to deliver coverage across different viewing options in the United States and Puerto Rico.Bids must be submitted by midnight on November 19, according to FIFA.

news.title: Supported by ‘vast, vast majority’ of football: Infantino ahead of polls
news.lede: Geneva, Oct 24: FIFA’s embattled president Gianni Infantino said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of football, despite his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. Infantino is seeking re-election next year as the head of football’s world governing body in the face of attempts to force him to stand down in the wake of the divisive plan. He infuriated football leaders in Europe, North America and Asia over the proposal to sell profits in the World Cup through a commercial subsidiary. But in an interview released Saturday with the BBC at the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, Infantino brushed off doubts about him being able to continue as president.

news.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: England 'not thinking about points difference' before France game, says Brad O'Neill
news.lede: England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday. An opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga has left their hopes of reaching the semi-finals hanging by a thread, with points difference looking increasingly like the only way to progress. But head coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man matchday squad, a sign that he does not plan radical changes against a France team smarting from their 78-4 humbling by Samoa.
